220-1201.name: CompTIA A+ Core 1
220-1201.description: Entry-level certification covering mobile devices, networking, hardware, virtualization, and troubleshooting.

objectives.1.1: Given a scenario, monitor mobile device hardware and use appropriate replacement techniques.
objectives.1.2: Compare and contrast accessories and connectivity options for mobile devices.
objectives.1.3: Given a scenario, configure basic mobile device network connectivity and provide application support.
objectives.2.1: Compare and contrast Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) ports, protocols, and their purposes.
objectives.2.3: Summarize services provided by networked hosts.
objectives.2.5: Compare and contrast common networking hardware devices.
objectives.2.6: Given a scenario, configure basic wired/wireless small office/home office (SOHO) networks.
objectives.2.7: Compare and contrast internet connection types, network types, and their characteristics.
objectives.2.8: Explain networking tools and their purposes.
objectives.3.1: Compare and contrast display components and attributes.
objectives.3.2: Summarize basic cable types and their connectors, features, and purposes.
objectives.3.5: Given a scenario, install and configure motherboards, central processing units (CPUs), and add-on cards.
objectives.3.6: Given a scenario, install the appropriate power supply.
objectives.3.7: Given a scenario, deploy and configure multifunction devices/printers and settings.
objectives.3.8: Given a scenario, perform appropriate printer maintenance.
objectives.5.1: Given a scenario, troubleshoot motherboards, RAM, CPUs, and power.
objectives.5.2: Given a scenario, troubleshoot drive and RAID issues.
objectives.5.3: Given a scenario, troubleshoot video, projector, and display issues.
objectives.5.4: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common mobile device issues.
objectives.5.5: Given a scenario, troubleshoot network issues.
objectives.5.6: Given a scenario, troubleshoot printer issues.

modules.1.0: What Does an IT Specialist Do?
modules.6.0: Configuring Network Addressing and Internet Connections

questionBank.stem: A technician is replacing a laptop keyboard. Which tool is MOST appropriate for prying up keycaps or bezels without damaging plastic clips?
questionBank.explanation: A plastic spudger is a non-conductive prying tool designed to avoid scratching or cracking plastic housings and clips during disassembly.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following are valid mobile device management (MDM) policies? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: BYOD, COPE, and COBO are recognized MDM policy models. MYOD is not standard, and VDI is a different technology.

questionBank.stem: A smartphone requires charging every 2 hours under normal use. The battery is 3 years old. Which is the BEST first action?
questionBank.explanation: Batteries degrade over time and typically need replacement after 2-3 years of regular use.
options: Perform a factory reset of the device

questionBank.stem: Which network device operates at Layer 2 and forwards frames based on MAC addresses?
questionBank.explanation: A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards frames only to the appropriate port, isolating collision domains per port.

questionBank.stem: Match each network protocol to its OSI layer.
questionBank.explanation: Each protocol operates at a specific OSI layer.

questionBank.stem: Which tools are MOST helpful for diagnosing network problems? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: ping, ipconfig, tracert, and nslookup are networking tools. tasklist is for processes, not networking.

questionBank.stem: Which wireless frequency band offers greater range but is prone to interference from cordless phones and microwaves?
questionBank.explanation: 2.4 GHz has better range but shares spectrum with many consumer devices, causing more interference.

questionBank.stem: A device has been assigned the IP address 169.254.34.12. What does this indicate?
questionBank.explanation: The 169.254.0.0/16 range is reserved for APIPA, assigned when DHCP fails.

questionBank.stem: Which motherboard form factor is the smallest, commonly used in compact builds?
questionBank.explanation: Mini-ITX is the smallest standard form factor for compact builds.

questionBank.stem: Match each CPU socket type to its characteristic.
questionBank.explanation: LGA has pins on the socket; PGA has pins on the CPU.

questionBank.stem: Which are valid RAM configurations for a modern desktop PC? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: DDR4 and DDR5 are valid. SODIMM is for laptops, ECC needs special boards, mixing types not possible.

questionBank.stem: Which cooling method is more effective than air cooling for high-performance CPUs?
questionBank.explanation: Liquid cooling transfers heat more efficiently than air cooling for high-TDP CPUs.

questionBank.stem: Which RAID level mirrors data, providing redundancy but using only 50% capacity?
questionBank.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives for full redundancy at 50% capacity cost.

questionBank.stem: Which connector provides supplemental power directly to the CPU on modern motherboards?
questionBank.explanation: The EPS12V connector supplies dedicated power to the processor.

questionBank.stem: Which expansion slot is used for modern discrete graphics cards?
questionBank.explanation: PCIe x16 is the standard modern expansion slot for graphics cards.

questionBank.stem: Which storage interface used a wide ribbon cable and master/slave jumper configuration?
questionBank.explanation: PATA (IDE) used ribbon cables and jumper settings, now superseded by SATA and NVMe.

questionBank.stem: A thermal printer produces faded output. Which could cause this? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Thermal printers rely on heat. Faded output from worn head, old paper, or weak heating element.

questionBank.stem: Which cloud model delivers fully managed applications like Microsoft 365?
questionBank.explanation: SaaS delivers fully managed applications to end users.

questionBank.stem: Which hypervisor runs directly on physical hardware?
questionBank.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware for better performance.

questionBank.stem: VirtualBox running on Windows is which type of hypervisor?
questionBank.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors run as applications on top of an existing host OS.

questionBank.stem: A hard drive makes repetitive clicking and system fails to boot. Most likely cause?
questionBank.explanation: Clicking indicates mechanical failure of the actuator arm/read-write head.

questionBank.stem: After installing new RAM, PC fails to POST. Try FIRST?
questionBank.explanation: POST failure after RAM install is usually improper seating or incompatibility.

questionBank.stem: Wi-Fi adapter enabled but no connections. Check what? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Check physical/software toggles, drivers, router power. SSID and battery don't prevent connection.
options: Physical Wi-Fi switch or Airplane Mode
correctAnswer: Physical Wi-Fi switch or Airplane Mode

questionBank.stem: What is a primary reason for using a patch panel in conjunction with a switch?
questionBank.explanation: A patch panel simplifies cable organization and facilitates network management by acting as a central hub for terminating and labeling Ethernet cables. It supports scalability, troubleshooting, and reconfiguration without disturbing permanent cabling. Providing power to devices is the role of Power over Ethernet (PoE) switches or injectors, not patch panels. Enhancing wireless coverage requires wireless access points while protecting network traffic involves security protocols like TLS, WPA3, or VPN, not patch panels.
options: To simplify cable organization and facilitate network management
To provide power to devices connected through Ethernet cables
correctAnswer: To simplify cable organization and facilitate network management

questionBank.stem: What does a dBm measurement represent?
questionBank.explanation: dBm measures signal strength relative to 1 milliwatt (mW), with values closer to zero indicating stronger signals. It is not related to battery level, bandwidth capacity, or the power output of the analyzer itself but is a standard way to express the strength of wireless signals.
options: A signal strength ratio compared to 1 milliwatt (mW)
The amount of power output by the Wi-Fi analyzer
A measurement of the device's battery level
The bandwidth capacity of the network
correctAnswer: A signal strength ratio compared to 1 milliwatt (mW)

questionBank.stem: A technician is assisting the CISO in wirelessly transferring data between their smartwatch and their corporate PC. As the CISO's request uses two devices in close proximity, what network method has a limited range?
questionBank.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) is designed for very short-range communication, typically within a few meters, and is commonly used for connecting personal devices like a smartwatch and a computer. Technologies like Bluetooth are often used in PANs to facilitate data transfer between devices in close proximity. While Wi-Fi can be used for wireless communication, it is generally intended for longer ranges than a PAN and often supports multiple devices over a broader area, not just close proximity connections. A Local Area Network (LAN) can include both wired and wireless connections within a building or office space. However, it covers a much larger area than a PAN and typically connects multiple devices over a more extended range. A Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) is a subset of LAN and generally uses Wi-Fi to connect devices within a broader area, such as an office or building, rather than specifically enabling close-range communication between two personal devices.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of Bluetooth?
questionBank.explanation: Bluetooth is mainly used to connect peripheral devices (like headphones or speakers) to PCs and mobile devices and to share data over short distances. Bluetooth is not designed for long-distance data transmission; that would require different wireless technology. It also doesn't provide Internet access, which Wi-Fi typically handles. Object tracking with encoded tags is performed by RFID, not Bluetooth.
options: To connect peripheral devices and share data over short distances
To enable high-speed, long-distance data transmission between buildings
To track objects using encoded tags for inventory management
To serve as the main technology for wireless Internet access
correctAnswer: To connect peripheral devices and share data over short distances

questionBank.stem: Why might an active network tap be used instead of a passive tap?
questionBank.explanation: An active network tap regenerates signals, which is essential for high-speed links, such as gigabit Ethernet over copper, where signal complexity exceeds passive tap capabilities. Passive taps are unpowered and simpler but may not support advanced signaling needs. Active taps do not filter corrupt frames, as they forward all data like passive taps. While active taps can be used with fiber, they are not exclusive to fiber connections.
options: Because active taps work without power, making them reliable in power outages
Because active taps are exclusively used for fiber optic connections
Because active taps filter out corrupt or malformed frames before sending data to the monitor
Because active taps regenerate signals, which is necessary for complex or high-speed links
correctAnswer: Because active taps regenerate signals, which is necessary for complex or high-speed links

questionBank.stem: Which of the following technologies does the 802.11ac wireless networking standard use to provide increased bandwidth and communication speeds? (Select two.)
questionBank.explanation: The 802.11ac wireless network standard increases bandwidth and communication speeds using the following technologies: MU-MIMO is an enhancement to MIMO that allows multiple users to use the same channel. In addition to adding MU-MIMO, 802.11ac doubled the number of MIMO radio streams from four to eight. Channel bonding combines two non-overlapping 20 MHz channels into a single 40 MHz channel, resulting in slightly more than double the bandwidth. All the other technologies are not used to increase the bandwidth and communication speeds for 801.11ac.
options: MU-MIMO to allow multiple users to access the same channel
OFDM modulation to allow several parallel data channels to stream data
Dual-band transmission to allow data to be transmitted at two frequencies at the same time
Channel bonding to combine more channels in the 5 GHz band to allow more than double the bandwidth
Peer-to-peer mode to allow each host to communicate directly with other hosts
correctAnswer: MU-MIMO to allow multiple users to access the same channel
Channel bonding to combine more channels in the 5 GHz band to allow more than double the bandwidth

questionBank.stem: You are using a crimper to attach an RJ-45 connector to a Cat 6 UTP cable. You need to use the T568A standard to connect the individual wires to the connector. Which wire should you connect to pin 1?
questionBank.explanation: According to the T568A standard, the green with white wire should be connected to pin 1 on an RJ-45 connector.

questionBank.stem: What is the purpose of a patch panel?
questionBank.explanation: The patch panel serves as a centralized point where wall port cables are connected to Ethernet switch ports, allowing easy changes to network connections. Directly connecting computers to switches without a patch panel would limit flexibility in network management. Wireless devices do not require this cabling setup, as they connect via Wi-Fi. Patch panels do not supply power to devices (a PoE switch does); they organize and link network connections.
options: To provide a centralized point where wall port cables are connected to Ethernet switch ports
To serve as a power supply for connected devices
To allow wireless devices to access the network through cabling
To directly connect computers to the Ethernet switch without additional components
correctAnswer: To provide a centralized point where wall port cables are connected to Ethernet switch ports

questionBank.stem: Which of the following are characteristics of a coaxial network cable? (Select two.)
questionBank.explanation: A coaxial cable is composed of a central copper conductor that is surrounded by an insulator, which is then surrounded by a second metallic mesh conductor. The name coaxial is derived from the fact that both of these conductors share a common axis. Twisted-pair cables are twisted around each other to reduce the effects of electromagnetic interference (EMI) and crosstalk. Fiber optic cables have a plastic or glass center (known as the core). Only fiber optic cables are totally immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI) because light pulses, instead of electrical signals, represent the data.
options: It uses two concentric metallic conductors.
It has conductors that are twisted around each other to eliminate crosstalk.
It has a conductor made from copper in the center.
It is totally immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI).
It is made of plastic or glass in the center.
correctAnswer: It uses two concentric metallic conductors.
It has a conductor made from copper in the center.

questionBank.stem: A printer is behaving erratically; you suspect a faulty parallel port. Which tool can you use to test the parallel port?
questionBank.explanation: A loopback plug allows an output signal to be returned as input. Loopback plugs are used to test serial and parallel ports. A cable tester verifies that a network can carry a signal from one end to the other and that all wires within the connector are in their correct positions. A multimeter measures electrical properties, such as voltage, amps, and resistance. An ammeter is an instrument that measures the flow of electric current in a circuit.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose for which loopback plugs are used?
questionBank.explanation: Loopback plugs are used to test ports by returning output signals as input. Use a loopback plug to test the functionality of serial ports or networking ports. A 3-prong holder is a tweezer-like tool with three prongs for grabbing and lifting small objects. An IC extractor is a tweezer-like tool (usually spring-loaded in the open position) that's used to remove integrated circuit chips. Null modem cables are used to connect computers using their serial ports without the need for a modem and phone line connection.
options: Testing ports by returning output signals as input
Connecting computers together without using network cards or modems
correctAnswer: Testing ports by returning output signals as input

questionBank.stem: Currently, your company is in the process of upgrading security in the company headquarters building by installing biometric sensors to limit access to specific rooms. Your network switches are PoE-enabled, which allows biometric sensors to connect to switches without an external power source. Which of the following PoE standards is designed for use with biometric sensors that require 25 watts?
questionBank.explanation: 802.3at PoE+ provides a maximum of 30 watts of power, which is designed for use with devices like biometric sensors and tablets. 802.3af POE allows powered devices to draw up to about 13 W. This is not enough watts for the device. 802.1X is a network access control/authentication standard, not a power-delivery standard. It governs how devices authenticate to the network; it does not define how power is delivered over Ethernet. 802.11n is a wireless networking standard (Wi-Fi) and is unrelated to PoE.

questionBank.stem: All the employees in a lawyer's office communicate with the internet and each other through the same appliance. What kind of network is the office using?
questionBank.explanation: A Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) network is designed for small office environments where a single appliance, such as a router, provides internet access and facilitates communication between devices within the office. This setup is common in small offices like a lawyer's office, where a simple, centralized network structure is sufficient. Zigbee is a wireless protocol used for low-power, low-data-rate communication in applications like home automation and IoT devices. It is not typically used for standard office networking and internet communication. A Personal Area Network (PAN) connects personal devices over a short range, usually for a single person (e.g., connecting a smartphone to a smartwatch). It does not describe a network that allows all office employees to communicate with each other and the internet. A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) covers a large geographic area, such as a city, and is used to connect multiple locations or buildings rather than the internal network of a single office.

questionBank.stem: You are designing a wireless network for a client. Your client needs the network to support a data rate of at least 150 Mbps. In addition, the client already has a wireless telephone system installed that operates at 2.4 GHz. Which 802.11 standard works BEST in this situation?
questionBank.explanation: 802.11n is the best choice for this client, as 802.11n supports both 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz with a maximum transmission rate of 600 Mbps. 802.11b and 802.11g both operate in the 2.4 GHz to 2.4835 GHz range, which causes interference with the client's wireless phone system. 802.11a operates in the 5.725 GHz to 5.850 GHz frequency range, which doesn't interfere with the phone system. However, the maximum speed is limited to 54 Mbps.

questionBank.stem: What is one of the main advantages of Wi-Fi 7's Multi-Link Operation (MLO)?
questionBank.explanation: Multi-Link Operation (MLO) in Wi-Fi 7 enables devices to send data over multiple bands (2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz) or channels, which helps reduce latency and improves throughput. MLO does not restrict data transfer to a single band but rather enhances flexibility and speed by using multiple bands. MLO does not limit connection speeds; instead, it optimizes performance. Wi-Fi 7 operates across various bands, not just 2.4 GHz, allowing better compatibility and speed.
options: It restricts data transfer to a single band for stability.
It allows devices to send data over multiple bands or channels.
It only operates in the 2.4 GHz band to support legacy devices.
It limits connection speeds to prevent network congestion.
correctAnswer: It allows devices to send data over multiple bands or channels.

questionBank.stem: What is the purpose of bonding multiple Ethernet NIC ports?
questionBank.explanation: Bonding multiple Ethernet NIC ports enables a higher-speed link by combining the individual speeds of each port, effectively increasing the data transfer rate. Improved signal quality for long distances is achieved through cabling standards or signal boosters, not by bonding ports. Using one port as a backup would be achieved through redundancy settings, not bonding, and simultaneous copper and fiber connections requiring specific NICs with different port types rather than bonded ports.
options: To create a higher-speed link by combining the speeds of multiple ports
To improve signal quality for distant connections
To connect both copper and fiber connections simultaneously
To allow one port to function as a backup in case of a failure
correctAnswer: To create a higher-speed link by combining the speeds of multiple ports

questionBank.stem: Which of the following network types uses special hardware to provide high-speed access to storage across the network?
questionBank.explanation: A storage area network (SAN) is a special type of network that provides high-speed access to storage across the network. Specialized hardware is used to store and provide access to needed data. In a peer-to-peer network, each host can provide network resources to other hosts or access resources located on other hosts. It does not use special hardware to provide high-speed access to storage across the network. A local area network is a network in a small geographic area, like an office. A LAN typically uses wires to connect systems together. It does not use special hardware to provide high-speed access to storage across the network. In a client-server network, hosts have specific roles. For example, some hosts are assigned server roles, which allow them to provide network resources to other hosts. Other hosts are assigned client roles, which allow them to consume network resources. It does not use special hardware to provide high-speed access to storage across the network.

questionBank.stem: Which type of network is best suited for a company that operates across multiple locations in a city?
questionBank.explanation: A MAN (Metropolitan Area Network) is ideal for a company with networks spread across multiple locations in a single city, as it bridges the gap between local LANs and broader WANs. LANs are restricted to a single site, PANs cover very small areas, and WLANs are limited to local, often indoor, wireless communication.

questionBank.stem: What best describes a Local Area Network (LAN)?
questionBank.explanation: A LAN is defined as a group of computers connected within a limited geographic location, like a building or campus. This distinguishes it from larger networks, like WANs, which span larger geographic areas. The other options refer to networks with broader coverage or specific functionalities, such as storage or city-wide coverage.
options: A specialized network dedicated to data storage
A group of computers connected within a close geographic location
A network that covers a city or municipality
A network that spans multiple geographic locations worldwide
correctAnswer: A group of computers connected within a close geographic location

questionBank.stem: What does an Ethernet switch use to forward frames to the correct destination?
questionBank.explanation: An Ethernet switch forwards frames based on the MAC address, which uniquely identifies devices on a local network. It uses a MAC address table to map addresses to specific ports. IP addresses operate at the network layer, but switches operate at the data link layer (Layer 2) and do not use IP addresses for forwarding frames. Port numbers and VLAN IDs are used for higher-level functions, such as routing and segmentation, but they are not involved in the basic operation of frame forwarding in switches.

questionBank.stem: A technician is running a network above a dropped ceiling that is also used for ventilation. The cable must be a twisted pair and must be capable of Gigabit Ethernet speeds. Which of the following cables should the technician use?
questionBank.explanation: Plenum-rated Cat 6a cables can transfer data at 10 Gbps and can be placed in plenum spaces used for ventilation. Riser-rated RG-58 cables are coaxial and can transfer data at 10 Mbps. Plenum-rated cables can be used in riser applications, but riser-rated cables cannot be used in plenum applications. Riser-rated Cat 5e cables can transfer data at 1 Gbps, but they cannot be used in plenum applications. Plenum-rated multimode fiber can transfer data at 10 Gbps, but it is not a twisted pair.

questionBank.stem: As a network engineer, you have been creating patch (straight-through) cables for a network switch. You have plugged in all the cables and are testing data transmission through the cables. You notice that the data transmission is not functioning properly in some of the cables, and you are sure that one of the cables is interfering with the transmission at the near end. What is this type of interference called?
questionBank.explanation: Cross-talk is an interference between two pairs in a cable. The cable transmitting the interfering signal interferes the greatest at the end where the interfering signal is transmitted from (called the near end) with other cables next to it. In this scenario, you probably did not keep the wire pairs twisted as much as possible up to the end of the cable connector, and you will need to fix the issue. Cat 5 Ethernet is a type of network connector, not a type of network interference. You are using a network switch, not a router, so there should be no interference from any router. Wi-Fi interference can come from many sources, but you are using a wired (not a wireless) connection.

questionBank.stem: Why can fiber optic cables support higher bandwidth and longer distances compared to copper cables?
questionBank.explanation: Fiber optic cables use light pulses that are not affected by electrical interference and suffer less attenuation, allowing for higher bandwidth and longer distances. Fiber optic cables are not necessarily thicker, as core size varies with the type of fiber. Copper signals are more susceptible to interference, limiting the distance they can travel. Fiber optics are durable but fragile in certain conditions and do not require longer runs based on durability.
options: Fiber optic cables are thicker, which reduces interference.
The light pulses in fiber optics are not susceptible to interference and experience less attenuation.
Fiber optic cables are less durable and, therefore, require longer cable runs.
Copper signals are stronger than light pulses, leading to shorter cable runs.
correctAnswer: The light pulses in fiber optics are not susceptible to interference and experience less attenuation.

questionBank.stem: What distinguishes single-mode fiber (SMF) from multi-mode fiber (MMF) in terms of usage?
questionBank.explanation: Single-mode fiber is designed for high-speed, long-distance transmission and is well-suited for WANs, while multi-mode fiber, with a larger core and LED-based technology, is cost-effective and ideal for shorter distances in LANs. Multi-mode does not use high-power lasers like SMF and is generally less capable of high-speed, long-distance transmission. SMF has a smaller core, focusing light more precisely, which improves distance and speed.
options: SMF has a larger core than MMF, allowing for more light to pass through.
SMF and MMF perform identically, with only minor cost differences.
SMF uses lower-cost LEDs, while MMF uses high-power lasers.
SMF is better suited for long distances and high speeds, whereas MMF is ideal for shorter distances in LANs.
correctAnswer: SMF is better suited for long distances and high speeds, whereas MMF is ideal for shorter distances in LANs.

questionBank.stem: A network technician needs to deploy a computer on an Ethernet network and notices that the computer will sit on a shelf directly under a fluorescent light. What type of cable will the technician use?
questionBank.explanation: Shielded Twisted Pair (STP) cable is the best choice for this situation because it includes shielding that protects against electromagnetic interference (EMI), which can be caused by fluorescent lighting. The shielding around the wires helps to prevent data transmission issues that could arise from the nearby light source. UTP lacks shielding, making it more susceptible to interference from nearby sources like fluorescent lights. This interference could lead to data loss or signal degradation, making UTP unsuitable in this environment. While coaxial cables are shielded and can resist some interference, they are not commonly used for standard Ethernet networks and are generally more suitable for television and broadband internet connections. Fiber optic cables are immune to electromagnetic interference; however, they are typically more expensive and may be unnecessary in this scenario where STP can provide sufficient protection. Fiber optic is generally reserved for long-distance or high-bandwidth applications.

questionBank.stem: What is a major benefit STP provides that UTP does not?
questionBank.explanation: Shielded twisted pair (STP) has a grounded outer copper shield around the bundle of twisted pairs or around each pair. This provides added protection against EMI. Unshielded twisted pair (UTP) does not have a grounded outer copper shield. STP costs considerably more than UTP. Neither is safer for installations in overhead ceiling spaces unless they are made with plenum plastic shielding. STP and UTP are equally effective at transmitting signals over the same distance.
options: Safer for installations in overhead ceiling spaces
Ability to install longer cable lengths

questionBank.stem: A network technician needs to replace a broken Ethernet cable. What connector will the technician use to terminate the new cable, also known as 8P8C?
questionBank.explanation: RJ-45 is the connector used to terminate Ethernet cables and is also known as an 8P8C (8-position, 8-contact) connector. This connector type is standard for Ethernet networking cables, enabling proper data transmission across devices on a network. F-type connectors are used for coaxial cables, primarily in television and cable internet connections, not for Ethernet cables. SC (Subscriber Connector or Standard Connector) is a type of fiber optic connector, not suitable for Ethernet cables, which use copper wiring. LC (Lucent Connector) is another type of fiber optic connector used for smaller form factor fiber optic cables, but it is also not appropriate for Ethernet cabling.

questionBank.stem: What is the primary function of a network tap?
questionBank.explanation: The main function of a network tap is to intercept and copy signals passing over a cable, enabling the captured data to be sent to a packet or protocol analyzer for monitoring or analysis. Amplifying signals for longer distances is not the purpose of a tap; this would involve repeaters or amplifiers. Network taps do not add additional connection ports for devices like a switch would, nor are they intended to replace switches in small networks.
options: To amplify signals passing over a cable for longer transmission distances
To provide additional ports for connecting multiple network devices
To replace network switches in small networks
To intercept and copy signals passing over a cable for monitoring or analysis
correctAnswer: To intercept and copy signals passing over a cable for monitoring or analysis

questionBank.stem: A network technician used a tool that energizes each wire in a cable. When the technician sent energy to some of the wires, the LED on the tool did not light up. What tool was the technician using?
questionBank.explanation: A cable tester is a tool used to check the integrity and functionality of cables by sending a signal through each wire. If the LED on the tester does not light up for certain wires, it indicates a break or fault in those wires, meaning the cable is not transmitting signals properly. A toner probe is used in conjunction with a tone generator to trace cables through walls or ceilings. It does not test the functionality of each wire within a cable. A tone generator, used with a probe, helps locate cables by emitting a tone. It is not designed to test the individual wires in a cable for continuity or signal integrity. A loopback plug is used to test network ports and troubleshoot connectivity issues by reflecting signals back to the source. It is not used to check the integrity of each individual wire in a cable.

questionBank.stem: A network technician is connecting a computer to the network using Ethernet. How is the physical connection to the cable made?
questionBank.explanation: The physical connection to an Ethernet cable is made via an RJ45 port, which is the standard port for Ethernet networking. An RJ45 connector on the Ethernet cable plugs directly into the RJ45 port on a computer or network device, allowing it to connect to the network. The MAC address is a unique identifier assigned to a network device, not a physical means of connection. It operates at the data link layer (Layer 2) and does not involve physically connecting the cable. A patch panel is a central point where network cables are organized and connected. However, it does not directly connect a computer to an Ethernet cable; instead, it helps manage multiple connections within a network setup. Power over Ethernet (PoE) allows Ethernet cables to transmit electrical power along with data, enabling devices like IP cameras or wireless access points to operate without separate power sources. It is not a method for physically connecting a computer to an Ethernet network.

questionBank.stem: A maintenance worker accidentally nicks a bundle of network cables routed to multiple wall jacks in a conference room. Only one of the cable's wires is severed. A technician is tasked with replacing the cable. Which of the following tools would the technician MOST likely use to identify which wall jack connects to the severed cable?
questionBank.explanation: A tone generator and probe can be used to identify the wall jack connected to the severed wire. The tone generator can be attached to the severed wire, and the probe will sound when it is brought close to the connected wall jack. A multimeter measures voltage, current, and resistance on a wire. A loopback plug can be plugged into a network adapter to test whether the NIC can send and receive properly. A cable stripper is used to cut away the plastic jacket or coating from a network cable.

questionBank.stem: A technician determines that an older network hub that connects 24 workstations is performing poorly due to excessive network collisions. Which of the following network devices would be the BEST replacement?
questionBank.explanation: A switch maintains a table of MAC addresses by port and forwards network data packets to only the port that matches the MAC address. This significantly reduces collisions. A router manages IP traffic between networks. A bridge separates two network segments and forwards data packets from one segment to another. A patch panel organizes network cables and connects inbound and outbound cables.

questionBank.stem: You are using a patch panel to connect the computers in your building to the appropriate switches, and you need to connect the Ethernet wires from the building network port cables to the patch panel. Where do you connect the wires on a patch panel?
questionBank.explanation: All network ports in a building terminate at a patch panel. The Ethernet cables are punched down and terminate on the backside of the patch panel. The front of the patch panel consists of RJ-45 ports. An Ethernet cable runs from the patch panel to the network switch to provide the connection between a device that is connected to the network port and the switch. There are no specified incoming or outgoing wires on an Ethernet cable.
options: You connect the incoming wires to the front and the outgoing wires to the back.
You connect the outgoing wires to the front and the incoming wires to the back.
You connect the wires to the backside of the panel.
You connect the wires to the front side of the panel.
correctAnswer: You connect the wires to the backside of the panel.

questionBank.stem: What component allows PoE functionality when a switch does not support PoE?
questionBank.explanation: A PoE injector (also known as a midspan device) enables PoE functionality when a switch does not natively support it. It connects between the switch and the powered device, injecting power into the Ethernet cable while preserving data connectivity. An endspan switch is a PoE-enabled switch that directly provides power without requiring additional hardware, which is different from using an injector. A power adapter provides local power to a device but does not integrate with Ethernet cabling. An Ethernet splitter splits network signals but does not provide power delivery, making it unsuitable for PoE functionality.

questionBank.stem: What differentiates a managed switch from an unmanaged switch?
questionBank.explanation: A managed switch can be configured with security settings and advanced features, offering greater control and functionality for larger networks. Unlike unmanaged switches, it provides options for network management and monitoring. Managed switches are not limited to specific ISPs and are specifically designed to connect devices within a network. They also come with physical ports for network connections, often in large quantities.
options: A managed switch operates only with a specific ISP's network.
A managed switch does not connect devices within a network.
A managed switch can be configured with security settings and advanced features.
A managed switch has no physical ports for network connections.
correctAnswer: A managed switch can be configured with security settings and advanced features.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following describes a benefit of using a patch panel?
questionBank.explanation: A patch panel prevents wear and tear on switch ports by serving as a static termination point for structured cabling. Short patch cables are used to connect the panel to the switch, making replacements easy without disturbing permanent cabling. Signal amplification is not a feature associated with patch panels. Switches are still required for network connectivity between connected devices. Patch panels do not reduce the number of cables needed; they simply organize them more effectively.
options: It eliminates the need for switches.
It amplifies signals over long distances.
It prevents wear and tear on switch ports.
It reduces the need for network cables.
correctAnswer: It prevents wear and tear on switch ports.

questionBank.stem: Why is it important to label ports on a patch panel?
questionBank.explanation: Labeling ports reduces errors during troubleshooting by making it easy to identify and match connections between the patch panel and switch. Proper labeling also speeds up network changes and repairs. Increasing network speed depends on hardware specifications, not labeling. Providing redundancy involves backup devices or paths, not labeling. Data collisions are eliminated by switches, which provide separate collision domains, not by labeling.
options: To provide redundancy in case of failure

questionBank.stem: How do switches and bridges learn where devices are located on a network?
questionBank.explanation: Bridges and switches learn addresses by copying the MAC address of the source device from the data packet header and placing it in the MAC address table. The port number the data packet entered is also recorded in the table and associated with the source MAC address. A switch and/or bridge cannot record the destination MAC address because they do not know the port that is used to reach the destination device. Bridges and switches operate at Layer 2 and do not use IP addresses (which exist at Layer 3).
options: When a data packet enters a port, the source IP address is copied from the data packet header.
When a data packet enters a port, the source MAC address is copied from the data packet header.
When a data packet enters a port, the destination IP address is copied from the data packet header.
When a data packet enters a port, the destination MAC address is copied from the data packet header.
correctAnswer: When a data packet enters a port, the source MAC address is copied from the data packet header.

questionBank.stem: What function does an Ethernet switch perform when it receives a data frame?
questionBank.explanation: An Ethernet switch decodes the frame to identify both the source and destination MAC addresses and then forwards the frame to the port that corresponds to the destination MAC address in its table. This process makes data delivery more efficient by only sending data to the intended recipient, unlike broadcasting, which sends data to all connected devices. Broadcasting frames to all ports is inefficient and is characteristic of network hubs, not switches. Ethernet switches forward frames in real-time as long as the destination MAC address is known. Discarding frames without an entry in the MAC address table is incorrect because switches will flood the frame to all ports except the source, learning new addresses as responses are received.
options: It decodes the frame and forwards it to the appropriate port based on the destination MAC address.
It broadcasts the frame to all ports.
It discards the frame if the destination is not in its MAC address table.
It stores the frame until the destination device requests it.
correctAnswer: It decodes the frame and forwards it to the appropriate port based on the destination MAC address.

questionBank.stem: Which IEEE PoE standard is most suitable for devices requiring around 25 W of power, such as advanced wireless access points and pan-tilt-zoom security cameras?
questionBank.explanation: 802.3at (PoE+ or Type 2) provides up to 25 W of power, making it ideal for devices with higher energy demands like advanced wireless access points, pan-tilt-zoom security cameras, and video IP phones. 802.3af only supports up to 13 W, which is insufficient for these higher-power devices. 802.3bt Type 3 and Type 4 standards deliver even more power, up to 51 W and 73 W, respectively, and are intended for significantly larger power requirements, such as digital signage and LED lighting, which exceed the needs of devices covered under 802.3at.

questionBank.stem: What is the purpose of a patch cord?
questionBank.explanation: A patch cord connects a port on the patch panel to a port on the Ethernet switch, completing the link from the wall port to the network. The computer connects to the wall port, not directly via the patch cord, to the ethernet switch. Terminating cables into IDCs is done at the back of the patch panel, not by the patch cord. While patch cords connect devices, they are not specifically used for routing network traffic between floors.
options: It routes network traffic between different floors in a building.
It links a port on the patch panel to a port on the Ethernet switch.
It terminates cables into insulation displacement connectors (IDCs).
It connects the computer directly to the Ethernet switch.
correctAnswer: It links a port on the patch panel to a port on the Ethernet switch.

questionBank.stem: Why might a company choose to use modular switches in its network?
questionBank.explanation: Modular switches allow companies to interconnect multiple switch units via a fast communications backplane, enabling the management of many access ports in a compact design. Modular switches are typically mounted in racks for efficient space use. They do not limit device connections but rather facilitate large networks. Additionally, they do not provide wireless connectivity; they are specifically for wired networks.
options: To provide wireless connectivity to employees
To avoid using racks for network equipment
To limit the number of devices connected to the network
To interconnect multiple switch units through a fast backplane
correctAnswer: To interconnect multiple switch units through a fast backplane

questionBank.stem: Why does an Ethernet switch eliminate the negative effects of collisions in a network?
questionBank.explanation: An Ethernet switch eliminates collisions by assigning a separate collision domain to each port, allowing devices to communicate independently. This configuration ensures that each device connected to the switch operates in full-duplex mode, enabling simultaneous sending and receiving of data at the network's full speed. Reducing the number of devices does not address collisions, as collisions occur based on how traffic is handled, not the number of connections. Preventing devices from sending data simultaneously is unnecessary because full-duplex communication inherently supports simultaneous transmissions. Limiting data to avoid congestion relates to traffic management, not collision prevention, which is handled by creating isolated collision domains per port.
options: It limits the amount of data transmitted to avoid congestion.
It assigns a separate collision domain to each port.
It reduces the number of devices connected to the network.
It prevents devices from sending data at the same time.
correctAnswer: It assigns a separate collision domain to each port.

questionBank.stem: How do adapters supporting Bluetooth versions 3 and 4 achieve faster data transfer rates?
questionBank.explanation: Adapters supporting Bluetooth versions 3 and 4 can achieve faster data transfer rates by negotiating an 802.11 radio link, which allows for higher speeds when transferring large files. Increasing signal range does not directly impact speed, and Bluetooth does not use infrared technology. Doubling the frequency is not a method used to increase speed in Bluetooth connections.
options: By doubling the Bluetooth frequency to enhance speed
By negotiating an 802.11 radio link for large file transfers
By increasing the Bluetooth signal range
By using infrared technology for improved connectivity
correctAnswer: By negotiating an 802.11 radio link for large file transfers

questionBank.stem: What distinguishes NFC from RFID technology?
questionBank.explanation: NFC operates at short ranges (typically up to two inches) and can act as both a tag and a reader, enabling peer-to-peer communication, which is suitable for contactless payments and quick data exchanges. RFID is primarily used for tracking and inventory over longer distances. RFID is less common for contactless payments, and neither technology is intended for high-speed or long-range data transfer.
options: RFID is primarily used for contactless payments, while NFC is used for high-speed data transfer.
NFC is used for tracking parcels over long distances.
NFC operates at very short ranges and can function as both tag and reader.
NFC and RFID are both designed for long-range communication.
correctAnswer: NFC operates at very short ranges and can function as both tag and reader.

questionBank.stem: A network technician is upgrading the wireless network so that it can take advantage of "multiple input multiple output" (MIMO) to increase reliability and bandwidth. What standard is the technician upgrading the wireless network to?
questionBank.explanation: 802.11n was the first Wi-Fi standard to introduce MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) technology, which allows multiple antennas to transmit and receive data simultaneously. This increases the network's reliability, range, and bandwidth, making it suitable for environments that require enhanced performance. 802.11g is an older standard that does not support MIMO. It operates at 2.4 GHz and offers lower speeds and ranges compared to 802.11n. 802.11b is one of the earliest Wi-Fi standards and does not support MIMO. It has a limited range and operates at slower speeds. 802.11a operates at 5 GHz and offers higher speeds than 802.11b and 802.11g, but it does not support MIMO. It is primarily used for specific business applications requiring the 5 GHz band without MIMO capability.

questionBank.stem: A network technician is upgrading a grocery store's checkout lines with contactless payment devices. What type of wireless technology are the payment devices based on?
questionBank.explanation: NFC (Near Field Communication) is a wireless technology used in contactless payment systems. It enables secure, short-range communication between devices, such as payment terminals and contactless cards or smartphones, typically within a range of a few centimeters. 802.11a is a Wi-Fi standard used for wireless networking, not typically for secure, short-range communication required in contactless payments. Bluetooth is a wireless technology for short-range communication, but it is generally used for pairing devices over a slightly longer range than NFC and is not specifically optimized for secure contactless payments. While RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) is used for short-range identification and can sometimes be used in payment systems, NFC is specifically designed for secure, close proximity communication and is the primary technology in contactless payment systems.

questionBank.stem: What is Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) primarily designed for?
questionBank.explanation: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is designed specifically for small battery-powered devices, transmitting small amounts of data occasionally to conserve power. BLE is not intended for continuous high-bandwidth applications like video streaming or large file transfers. BLE is not backward compatible with classic Bluetooth, although some devices can support both BLE and classic Bluetooth simultaneously.
options: Small battery-powered devices that transmit small amounts of data infrequently
Continuous streaming of high-definition video content
Enabling backward compatibility with all previous Bluetooth versions
Large file transfers between computers and mobile devices
correctAnswer: Small battery-powered devices that transmit small amounts of data infrequently

questionBank.stem: What feature of Bluetooth allows two devices to securely exchange data?
questionBank.explanation: Bluetooth devices use a pairing procedure to authenticate each other, ensuring a secure connection before data exchange. Bluetooth connections are wireless, not requiring physical cables, and the pairing process rather than memory encryption is what ensures secure data exchange. Bluetooth can connect different types of devices, not just identical ones.
options: Pairing procedure that authenticates devices before communication
Encrypted data stored in the device's internal memory
Use of physical cables between devices
Only allowing communication between identical device types
correctAnswer: Pairing procedure that authenticates devices before communication

questionBank.stem: What is the advantage of using the same SSID for both frequency bands on a dual-band access point?
questionBank.explanation: Using the same SSID for both bands allows devices to automatically connect to the band with the strongest signal, improving connectivity and simplifying network selection for the user. Forcing devices to a specific band or requiring manual selection would limit flexibility. Using the same SSID does not inherently reduce interference from nearby networks, which is managed through channel configuration.
options: It forces devices to use only the 2.4 GHz band.
It restricts users to manual selection of the frequency band.
It prevents interference from nearby networks.
It allows devices to automatically connect to the band with the strongest signal.
correctAnswer: It allows devices to automatically connect to the band with the strongest signal.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following are characteristics of the 802.11g wireless standard? (Select three.)
questionBank.explanation: 802.11g wireless networks operate in the 2.4 GHz range, have a maximum bandwidth of 54 Mbps, and are backward compatible with 802.11b networks. 802.11b provides 11 Mbps of bandwidth. 802.11a operates in the 5.75 GHz range. For this reason, 802.11a is not compatible with 802.11b or 802.11g.

questionBank.stem: What does a high Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) indicate in a wireless network?
questionBank.explanation: A high Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) means the signal is significantly stronger than the background noise, leading to better network performance. Higher noise levels would result in a lower SNR, not a higher one. SNR does not reflect power output or directly relate to data speed but impacts the quality and reliability of the connection.
options: Increased power output from the Wi-Fi device
Low data transmission speed across the network
Higher noise levels that interfere with the signal
Stronger signal compared to background noise
correctAnswer: Stronger signal compared to background noise

questionBank.stem: An organization located on a large piece of rural property needs to connect its office building on the north side of the property with its warehouse and shipping operation on the south side of the property. The organization decides to connect the locations using long-range fixed wireless. What frequency spectrum must the organization use to ensure that nobody else can use the same frequency band?
questionBank.explanation: A licensed frequency spectrum provides exclusive access to a specific frequency band, ensuring that no other entities can use the same frequency in the area. This is especially useful for long-range, fixed wireless connections in rural areas where dedicated, interference-free communication is essential for reliable operation between distant locations. Unlicensed frequencies, such as the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, are open for public use, meaning that other organizations or individuals could potentially operate on the same frequencies, leading to interference and unreliable communication. 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) is a Wi-Fi standard, not a frequency spectrum type. It typically operates in unlicensed bands and is designed for high-density, short- to medium-range wireless networks, not long-range fixed wireless connections. DFS is a mechanism that allows Wi-Fi devices to avoid interference with radar systems by automatically selecting channels within the 5 GHz band. However, it does not provide exclusive access to frequencies, so other users could still be present on the same frequencies.

questionBank.stem: Which IEEE wireless standards specify transmission speeds up to 54 Mbps? (Select two.)
questionBank.explanation: Both the 802.11a and the 802.11g wireless standards specify maximum transmission speeds up to 54 Mbps. Bluetooth is a wireless standard that is commonly used to connect peripheral devices and operates at 720 Kbps. The 802.11b wireless standard provides transmission speeds of 11 Mbps. The 802.11ac wireless standard provides transmission speeds of up to 2.6 Gbps.

questionBank.stem: Which dBm value is the most realistic and indicates a strong wireless signal in a typical environment?
questionBank.explanation: -65 dBm is generally considered a strong wireless signal, suitable for reliable connectivity. A value of -90 dBm or -80 dBm is weaker and likely to result in packet loss or disconnections. A value of -30 dBm is extremely strong, but -65 dBm is typically the threshold for good performance in common wireless environments.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following wireless networking standards uses a frequency of 5 GHz and supports data transmission speeds up to 2.6 Gbps?
questionBank.explanation: The 802.11ac standard uses the 5 GHz frequency and supports data transmission speeds up to 2.6 Gbps. 802.11g and 802.11a both support data transmission speeds up to 54 Mbps. 802.11b supports data transmission speeds up to 11 Mbps. 802.11n supports data transmission speeds up to 600 Mbps.

questionBank.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Wi-Fi analyzer?
questionBank.explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer is used to measure the signal strength of various networks and troubleshoot performance issues, helping to identify optimal channel configurations. It does not boost signals, create new access points, or directly reduce noise; rather, it analyzes existing conditions to assist in optimizing network performance.
options: To create new wireless access points automatically
To measure signal strength and troubleshoot performance issues
To boost the signal strength of wireless networks
To reduce noise levels in wireless networks
correctAnswer: To measure signal strength and troubleshoot performance issues

questionBank.stem: A user reports that their desktop computer will not power on. You begin troubleshooting by "Questioning the Obvious." Which of the following actions would be the MOST appropriate first step?
questionBank.explanation: "Questioning the Obvious" involves starting with simple and obvious checks. Ensuring that the power cable is properly connected is a basic step that could resolve the issue without requiring more complex diagnostics. Replacing the power supply unit is a more advanced troubleshooting step. Before taking such action, you should perform basic checks, such as verifying the power cable connection, to rule out simpler causes. Inspecting the motherboard is a more detailed diagnostic step that should only be performed after ruling out simpler, more obvious causes like power cable issues or a faulty outlet. Escalation is only necessary if the problem cannot be resolved after performing basic troubleshooting steps. "Questioning the Obvious" focuses on addressing simple potential causes before involving senior staff.
options: Open the computer case and inspect the motherboard for physical damage.
Check if the power cable is securely connected to both the computer and the power outlet.
Escalate the issue to senior technical staff for further investigation.
Replace the computer's power supply unit with a new one.
correctAnswer: Check if the power cable is securely connected to both the computer and the power outlet.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following answers refer to the primary causes of port flapping? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Port flapping is caused by physical link instability or configuration mismatch.
options: Excessive traffic on a network device
Loose, faulty, or unsupported network cabling
correctAnswer: Loose, faulty, or unsupported network cabling

questionBank.stem: Which network issues are directly linked to port flapping? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Port flapping causes connectivity interruptions and speed degradation.

questionBank.stem: What is the recommended first step when troubleshooting port flapping?
questionBank.explanation: Start with physical connections per troubleshooting methodology.

questionBank.stem: What condition may lead to increased latency on a network?
questionBank.explanation: All factors contribute to network latency.
options: Network congestion due to excessive traffic
Physical distance between sender and receiver

questionBank.stem: Which solution has no direct impact on decreasing network latency?
questionBank.explanation: VLANs segment traffic but don't reduce latency within segments.
options: Using wired connections instead of wireless
Implementing VLANs to segment network traffic
Reducing physical distance between network devices
correctAnswer: Implementing VLANs to segment network traffic

questionBank.stem: Which type of network cabling is most susceptible to external interference?

questionBank.stem: Which network cabling provides immunity against external interference?
questionBank.explanation: Fiber optic uses light pulses immune to EMI.

questionBank.stem: For wireless client connection, security and encryption settings must match the WAP.

questionBank.stem: WAN signal loss logged during internet drops with good local connectivity. Next step?

questionBank.stem: Vertical lines in laser printer output indicate problem with:

Keep printer powered on and try another print job
Power cycle the printer after clearing jam

questionBank.stem: Common cause of faded laser printer output:
questionBank.explanation: Low toner produces faded output.

questionBank.explanation: Low ink and clogged printheads cause fading.

questionBank.stem: Causes of paper not feeding? (Select all)
questionBank.explanation: Multiple hardware and software factors affect feeding.

Worn or dirty paper feed rollers

questionBank.stem: Printer pulling multiple sheets - check for:
questionBank.explanation: All factors contribute to multi-sheet feed problems.

Check for paper jams in the printer

questionBank.stem: Most common causes of speckling on laser printed pages? (Select 3)

Partially clogged or dirty printhead nozzles

questionBank.stem: Dark spots on inkjet pages - probable causes? (Select 3)
questionBank.explanation: Debris, clogged heads, and leaking ink cause spots.

Partial blockages or dirt in printhead nozzles
correctAnswer: Excess paper dust, debris, or ink residue on the paper path
Partial blockages or dirt in printhead nozzles

questionBank.stem: Double images in laser printer caused by residual latent image on drum.
questionBank.explanation: Drum not cleaned between cycles creates echo images.

questionBank.stem: Grinding noise in inkjet - issues? (Select 3)
questionBank.explanation: Worn rollers, foreign objects, and carriage issues cause noise.

Small paper pieces or foreign objects stuck in the paper path
Worn or damaged gears and bearings affecting the drum unit
Faulty or worn fuser rollers and bearings

questionBank.stem: Grinding in laser printer - investigate? (Select all)
questionBank.explanation: Mechanical wear causes grinding in laser printers.

questionBank.explanation: Finishing includes staple jams and hole-punch waste management.

questionBank.stem: Least likely cause of printer not recognizing paper tray:
questionBank.explanation: Paper grade doesn't affect tray recognition.

Use of lower-grade, inexpensive, or recycled paper

questionBank.stem: Troubleshooting network printer connectivity - which helps:
questionBank.explanation: All troubleshooting steps are valuable for network printers.

Check the printer IP configuration settings

questionBank.stem: Least likely to solve frozen print queue:

questionBank.stem: While sideloading an app onto an Android phone for testing purposes, a user receives a notification that the installation has been blocked due to security settings. What must be changed to proceed with the installation?

Disable app verification in Google Play settings
Enable the Install unknown apps or Unknown sources setting
Turn on developer options in system settings

questionBank.stem: A company MDM administrator receives multiple tickets from users stating that they cannot install updates for existing apps or download new ones. Which of the following is the most likely reason?

questionBank.stem: A user reports the stylus has stopped responding on their touchscreen device. What is the first practical troubleshooting step a technician should try?

Clean the screen protector with a soft cloth

questionBank.stem: A device stylus functions intermittently, while the touchscreen responds normally to finger input. Which troubleshooting action should be considered first?

questionBank.stem: A user attempts to connect a Bluetooth stylus to their tablet but it does not appear in the device Bluetooth list. What device mode should the user confirm the stylus is in?

questionBank.stem: What factor(s) can contribute to unexpected performance drops on a mobile device? (Select all that apply)

questionBank.stem: A user complains their mobile phone has become increasingly slow, with apps taking a long time to open and frequently freezing. Which steps should a technician try first? (Select 2)

questionBank.stem: A mobile device experiences a sudden, significant drop in performance, accompanied by unusual pop-ups and battery drain. What is the most likely cause of the problem?

questionBank.stem: Wireless connectivity issues can be caused by physical obstructions and electronic interference. questionBank.stem: When troubleshooting intermittent wireless connectivity, what tool can a technician use to measure signal strength and detect potential dead zones?

questionBank.stem: A user laptop connects to the wireless network, but the connection is unstable and frequently drops, even after forcing reconnection and restarting the system. Check the router logs for unusual activity

Connect to a different Wi-Fi network

questionBank.stem: Which troubleshooting steps can help resolve intermittent wireless connectivity caused by external interference? (Select 2)

questionBank.stem: A user notices their online gaming experience suffers from high network latency and lag spikes. What common internal factors on their computer could explain these symptoms, particularly if they have many installed programs? (Select 2)

questionBank.stem: An administrator is troubleshooting a computer showing Limited Connectivity. The network icon displays an X symbol. Which actions should the administrator take first? (Select 2)

Run the built-in network diagnostics tool

questionBank.stem: A network admin can successfully ping a remote host by its IP address but cannot do so by its domain name. What is the most probable cause of this issue?
questionBank.explanation: Name resolution failure indicates DNS problem.

questionBank.stem: What is jitter in the context of network performance?
questionBank.explanation: Jitter is inconsistent packet timing.

questionBank.stem: Which network application types are most sensitive to jitter?
questionBank.explanation: Real-time apps require consistent timing.

questionBank.stem: During a VoIP call, a user hears their own voice echoing back to them with a slight delay. Which network performance issue is this symptom most indicative of?
questionBank.explanation: Echo with delay is characteristic of high latency.

questionBank.stem: What is the most likely cause of choppy or distorted audio during a VoIP call?
questionBank.explanation: Jitter causes audio distortion in real-time calls.

questionBank.stem: What is the primary purpose of a jitter buffer in VoIP systems?
questionBank.explanation: Jitter buffers compensate for packet timing variation.

questionBank.stem: The term Port flapping refers to a condition where a network port light, typically on a switch or router, rapidly alternates between up and down states. In such cases, the port status LED may blink erratically as it continuously loses and regains connection.
questionBank.explanation: Port flapping definition is accurate.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following actions are considered best practices for monitoring the health of a mobile device battery? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Battery health monitoring involves tracking degradation and checking for physical issues.
options: Always fully discharge the battery before recharging
Track battery health using built-in OS tools or third-party apps
Disable battery-saving features to get a more accurate reading of capacity loss
Monitor charging cycles and battery capacity degradation
Check for swelling, overheating, or failure to hold a charge
correctAnswer: Track battery health using built-in OS tools or third-party apps
Monitor charging cycles and battery capacity degradation
Check for swelling, overheating, or failure to hold a charge

questionBank.stem: Common battery types used in modern portable devices include: (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Li-ion and LiPo are standard in modern devices; older types like Ni-Cd are obsolete.

questionBank.stem: Which of the steps listed below should be followed when replacing a mobile device battery? (Select 3 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Safe battery replacement requires compatibility, proper procedure, and disposal.
options: Follow manufacturer guidelines for safe removal and installation
Ensure proper disposal of the old battery according to local regulations for electronic waste
Use any available universal battery as long as it fits physically within the device
Charge the new battery to 100% immediately after installation and then let it fully discharge to condition it
Ensure the replacement battery is compatible with the device model
correctAnswer: Follow manufacturer guidelines for safe removal and installation
Ensure proper disposal of the old battery according to local regulations for electronic waste
Ensure the replacement battery is compatible with the device model

questionBank.stem: Which laptop feature compensates for limited keyboard space by enabling additional functions on the same keys?
questionBank.explanation: Fn key provides secondary functions on standard keys.

questionBank.stem: Which action does not conform with recommended practices for diagnosing and repairing a mobile device keyboard?
questionBank.explanation: Device must be powered off during repair for safety.
options: Implement proper ESD safety measures by using an anti-static wristband and working on an ESD mat to protect sensitive components from static discharge
Perform comprehensive diagnostics using specialized key testing software to accurately identify any malfunctioning keys
Use appropriate tools (such as precision screwdrivers and plastic pry tools) and OEM-approved replacement parts to avoid causing further damage during the repair
Conduct detailed visual inspections to detect physical damage, debris accumulation, or water exposure on the keyboard
Follow manufacturer guidelines by consulting the service manual or official repair guide to ensure safe disassembly and reassembly of the device
Leave the device powered on during repair to provide immediate feedback on the exact malfunctioning component, such as a faulty key
correctAnswer: Leave the device powered on during repair to provide immediate feedback on the exact malfunctioning component, such as a faulty key

questionBank.stem: Which of the following devices generally offers the easiest and most user-accessible RAM replacement procedure?
questionBank.explanation: Laptops have user-accessible RAM; phones and tablets require disassembly.

questionBank.stem: Which of the tools listed below can be used to monitor the health and performance of a laptop storage drive?
questionBank.explanation: S.M.A.R.T. monitors drive health and predicts failures.

questionBank.stem: Which drive malfunction symptoms are not present in SSDs? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: SSDs have no moving parts; grinding and clicking are mechanical HDD issues.

questionBank.stem: What should be the preliminary step of an HDD/SSD replacement procedure?
questionBank.explanation: Always backup data before replacement.
options: Power down the device and remove the battery
Format the new drive before installing it
Perform a full system reset before replacing the drive
Backup the data on the existing drive
correctAnswer: Backup the data on the existing drive

questionBank.stem: What is the easiest method to monitor the wireless card performance in a mobile device?
questionBank.explanation: Signal strength indicator in notification area is easiest check.
options: Check the Wi-Fi signal strength icon in the device notification area
Observe any LED indicators for Wi-Fi status on the device
Perform an online speed test to measure the connection performance
Manually adjust the antenna position to improve signal strength
correctAnswer: Check the Wi-Fi signal strength icon in the device notification area

questionBank.stem: Which actions should be performed first when replacing a faulty wireless card/module in a laptop? (Select 2 answers)
questionBank.explanation: Power down and remove peripherals before opening device.
options: Power down the laptop and remove the battery
Label all screws and connectors during disassembly to aid reassembly
Remove all external peripherals from the device
Perform a full power cycle of the laptop by turning it off and then on again
Locate the wireless card slot on the motherboard
correctAnswer: Power down the laptop and remove the battery
Remove all external peripherals from the device

questionBank.stem: Which of the following statements regarding a mobile device Bluetooth module is true?
questionBank.explanation: Bluetooth is typically integrated into the main board.
options: Bluetooth modules are typically located near the device display and require screen removal for replacement
Once a Bluetooth module is replaced, it will automatically adjust to the device current settings without the need for manual pairing
Bluetooth is usually integrated into the Wi-Fi card or directly into the motherboard
When replacing a faulty Bluetooth module, as long as the physical connectors match, the new Bluetooth module can come from a different device model
correctAnswer: Bluetooth is usually integrated into the Wi-Fi card or directly into the motherboard

questionBank.stem: What is a recommended practice for assessing the effectiveness and reliability of biometric components on a mobile device?
questionBank.explanation: Multiple assessment methods provide comprehensive evaluation.
options: Using software tools to track scan success rates, response times, and error logs
Ensuring proper calibration through built-in settings or specialized diagnostic software
Tracking access attempts and failures for security auditing purposes
Updating drivers and firmware to prevent malfunctions caused by outdated software

questionBank.stem: After replacing a faulty biometric scanner on a mobile device, which essential step must be performed to ensure that the scanner produces accurate readings?
questionBank.explanation: Recalibration aligns the new scanner with device software.

questionBank.stem: A technician is troubleshooting a mobile device NFC functionality. Which action(s) would help verify the NFC scanner operational status? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Multiple checks ensure NFC is working properly.
options: Check for dirt or moisture on the sensor surface
Test the NFC functionality with a known compatible NFC tag or device
Update the device screen brightness, as the NFC sensor relies on ambient light levels
Connect to a Wi-Fi network to test device connectivity
Ensure NFC is enabled in the device settings
correctAnswer: Check for dirt or moisture on the sensor surface
Test the NFC functionality with a known compatible NFC tag or device
Ensure NFC is enabled in the device settings

questionBank.stem: Which of the answers listed below correctly describes the typical location of a laptop Wi-Fi antenna?
questionBank.explanation: Antennas are located at the top of display bezel.
options: Near the top, inside display case
Typically attached via external expansion port
correctAnswer: Near the top, inside display case

questionBank.stem: Which of the following actions would not help in troubleshooting a malfunctioning mobile device camera?
questionBank.explanation: Screen brightness does not affect camera operation.
options: Inspect and clean the camera lens
Test camera functionality in multiple apps
Adjust the host device screen brightness
Check for firmware and software updates
correctAnswer: Adjust the host device screen brightness

questionBank.stem: Which of the items listed below is not recommended for clearing potential blockages from a mobile device microphone?
questionBank.explanation: Compressed air can damage microphone diaphragm.

questionBank.stem: Examples of USB ports that can be found on mobile devices include: (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Modern phones use USB-C and older devices used Micro/Mini USB.

questionBank.stem: A type of USB connection method commonly used in modern mobile devices due to its reversible design, fast data transfer, and power capabilities is known as:
questionBank.explanation: USB-C is the modern standard for mobile devices.

questionBank.stem: Which proprietary connector was developed by Apple for its mobile devices?
questionBank.explanation: Lightning connector is proprietary to Apple devices.

questionBank.stem: NFC enables: (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: NFC supports multiple short-range communication uses.

questionBank.stem: Which of the following is a popular, short-range wireless standard for connecting various personal devices in a WPAN?
questionBank.explanation: Bluetooth is standard for WPAN connections.

questionBank.stem: Which of the terms listed below best describes a mobile device ability to share its Internet connection with other devices?
questionBank.explanation: Tethering shares mobile data with other devices.

questionBank.stem: A mobile hotspot is a device that creates a WLAN by acting as a portable WAP for other devices.
questionBank.explanation: Mobile hotspot definition is accurate.

questionBank.stem: Which are valid Windows 11 editions for corporate deployment? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Pro and Enterprise for corporate. Home is consumer. Standard and Professional Plus are invalid.

questionBank.stem: Where to configure network drive mapping in Windows?
questionBank.explanation: File Explorer provides 'Map Network Drive' feature for network share access.

questionBank.stem: Match Windows command-line tools to their function.
questionBank.explanation: ipconfig for network, tasklist for processes, diskpart for partitions, sfc for system files.

questionBank.stem: Windows system slow - which tool shows real-time CPU, memory, disk?
questionBank.explanation: Resource Monitor and Task Manager Performance tab show real-time system resource usage.

questionBank.stem: Which are strong password practices? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Mixed characters, MFA, and expiration are good. Reusing and writing down are security risks.

questionBank.stem: Workstation with malware - FIRST action in recovery?
questionBank.explanation: Isolate system first and document to prevent spread and enable analysis.

questionBank.stem: Which restricts user permissions to prevent system changes?
questionBank.explanation: UAC prompts for elevation on system-level changes.

questionBank.stem: Legitimate wireless security methods? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: WPA3, strong passwords, MAC filtering provide security. Disabling SSID is weak; 2.4 GHz reduces options.

questionBank.stem: Application crashes frequently. Try FIRST?
questionBank.explanation: Updates often fix bugs. Try this before drastic measures.

questionBank.stem: Order the troubleshooting steps correctly.
questionBank.explanation: Proper order: gather, theory, test, implement, verify.

questionBank.stem: Browser homepage changed without permission. Possible causes? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Hijackers, adware, extensions can change homepage. OS/driver updates don't.

questionBank.stem: Documentation after resolving ticket should include?
questionBank.explanation: Complete documentation helps others resolve similar issues.

questionBank.stem: Proper change management procedures? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: Test, document, notify, have rollback. Changes during maintenance windows, not peak hours.

questionBank.stem: Backup system never tested - PRIMARY concern?
questionBank.explanation: Untested backups create false security. Regular restoration testing is critical.

questionBank.stem: Environmental safety and compliance measures? (Select all that apply)
questionBank.explanation: E-waste disposal, ESD, battery storage, data handling are compliance. Indefinite reuse is not best practice.

questionBank.stem: Which can result in authentication failure with correct credentials?
questionBank.explanation: All factors prevent successful authentication.
